newsitem.title: ITALY: U.S. says EU not subsidising wheat aggressively.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says EU not subsidising wheat aggressively.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on Friday following talks with the European Union's farm commissioner Franz Fischler that the EU was honouring a commitment not to undercut U.S. wheat prices and was not using wheat export subsidies aggressively.
But he reiterated after talks with Fischler in Rome on Thursday night that while the United States had no present plans to reintroduce its own subsidies, such a decision had not been ruled out.

"We felt that they were honouring their commitments," Glickman told a news conference, referring to recent EU pledges not to sell wheat for less than the price of soft red winter wheat grown in the United States.

He welcomed an EU decision to lower its wheat export refunds at a weekly auction on Thursday in response to a smaller gap between U.S. and European prices. Glickman and Fischler were in Rome for the U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit.
"They indicated to us that they did not intend to aggressively use export susbidies to compete in export markets but we gave no commitments on our own export subsidies," he said.

He said that the Export Enhancement Programme (EEP) of wheat subsidies to U.S. farmers, which has not been used since 1995, was primarily designed to protect the U.S. from unfair trade practices by other governments.
